newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mining industry source doubts Busang leak report.
newsitem.headline: Mining industry source doubts Busang leak report.

text.p: A Jakarta newspaper on Tuesday said leaked results of drill tests at the Busang gold property showed the site held "cheerful" grades of gold, but an industry source said he doubted the accuracy of the report.

The source, who is close to the property, said the assaying of core samples from six test drills by a Canadian mining consultant was under very tight wraps and he did not believe there had been a leak.
The newspaper, Harian Ekonomi Neraca, said the results of the independent audit by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd did not indicate the size of the deposit.
"If not mistaken, it (the audit) only states that Busang contained gold grades whose prospects were cheerful," the daily quoted an unidentified source as saying.

Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which holds 45 percent of the main Busang II site, is expected to release the assay results after the Toronto Stock Exchange closes on Friday, the industry source added.
But Bre-X only said on April 26 that it expected to issue an interim report on the findings later this week.
Bre-X stunned the world last month when it said there was a strong possibility that the potential gold resources contained in the Busang property might have been overstated.
Bre-X had previously estimated Busang to contain some 70.95 million ounces of gold, making it this century's biggest find.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the United States has 15 percent and Indonesian interests the remaining 40 percent of the Busang II property.
The industry source said two of the three laboratories assaying the Busang ore samples for Strathcona had completed their task.
"I heard that two of the laboratories have completed their assays," the source said. "But it is not clear whether they are the ones in Indonesia, Canada or Australia."
The samples are being assayed by PT Indo Assay in the East Kalimantan town of Balikpapan, and laboratories in Perth and Vancouver. Their names have not been revealed.

Freeport said in a statement in late March it would participate in the development of the project only if developing the find was economically feasible. Freeport has also said its own independent test drillings at Busang had found insignificant amount of gold.
Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana told reporters on Monday the government had not received any report from Freeport regarding its intentions to withdraw from the project.
Neraca reported on Tuesday that there was talk that Canada's Placer Dome would replace Freeport if the U.S. mining giant pulled out of the project.
When contacted, John Loney, president-director of PT Placer Emas Indonesia, a unit of Placer Dome, said the company had no interest in Busang at the moment.
"I think it is speculation. We have no interest in Busang at the moment," he told Reuters.
